The house is famously recognized as the backdrop for the filming of “I Don’t Like,” one of the songs and visuals that helped turn Keef into one of the most influential figures to emerge from Chicago’s drill scene.

source_caption_text:
#ChiefKeef was recently back at his grandmother’s house in Chicago, arriving with bulletproof trucks — the same location that holds a major piece of his early history. The house is famously recognized as the backdrop for the filming of “I Don’t Like,” one of the songs and visuals that helped turn Keef into one of the most influential figures to emerge from Chicago’s drill scene.

Years later, seeing Keef back at the same place where some of those early moments were captured hits differently. From filming in the neighborhood as a teenager to becoming a global name, his return is a reminder of just how far his career and influence have traveled.

Same city. Same roots. Different level.
